questions.text: Government portal ease of finding — Ease of finding the government portal is understood as being found on the first result page of the three most popular search engines used in the country, this can be checked by accessing http://gs.statcounter.com/browser-market-share to see which are the most popular search engines

questions.title: Advanced search options
questions.text: Advanced search options — Advanced search options may include features that allow users to run custom searches with specific text, indicate unwanted words, specify date ranges, language options, etc. There can also be options available to refine the results after the search page.
questions.what: Advanced search options may include features that allow users to run custom searches with specific text, indicate unwanted words, specify date ranges, language options, etc. There can also be options available to refine the results after the search page.
questions.why: It allows users to refine their queries, enabling precise and efficient access to specific information or services, enhancing user satisfaction and usability.

questions.title: Sitemap/Index
questions.text: Sitemap/Index — A sitemap or index has a list of pages of a web site accessible to users. It is a web page that lists all the available pages within the website, typically organized in a hierarchical fashion. This helps visitors and search engine bots find pages on the site.
questions.what: A sitemap or index has a list of pages of a web site accessible to users. It is a web page that lists all the available pages within the website, typically organized in a hierarchical fashion. This helps visitors and search engine bots find pages on the site.
questions.why: Crucial as it provides a structured, organized map of the website's content, making it easier for visitors and search engines to navigate and access relevant information efficiently.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Choose the Right Format: a. Decide between an XML sitemap (for search engines) and an HTML sitemap (for users). XML sitemaps are essential for search engines, while HTML sitemaps serve as user-friendly guides. 2. Link from Website Footer: a. Add a link to the HTML sitemap in the footer section of your website. 3. Submit XML Sitemap to Search Engines: a. Submit the XML sitemap to search engines like Google and Bing through their respective webmaster tools. This helps search engines crawl and index your site more effectively. 4. Update Sitemap Regularly: a. Keep the XML sitemap updated whenever you add new pages For more information check out Google's guide.

questions.title: Accessibility by citizens/businesses to own data
questions.text: Accessibility by citizens/businesses to own data — Defined as the ability for users to access their own data (that government has on record), on the government portal, such as (but not limited to) data on social security, vehicle registration, etc. This usually requires authentication with a digital ID.
questions.what: Defined as the ability for users to access their own data (that government has on record), on the government portal, such as (but not limited to) data on social security, vehicle registration, etc. This usually requires authentication with a digital ID.
questions.why: Ensures transparency, fosters public trust, and empowers people to access their own information, promoting accountability and civic engagement.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Review Privacy Laws: a. Understand laws governing the accessibility and protection of personal/Business data. 2. Implement Secure Authentication: a. Require strong, multi-factor authentication for users accessing personal/business data. Use encrypted connections (SSL/TLS) to protect data in transit. 3. User Verification: a. Verify the identity of users before granting access to personal data. 4. Data Minimization: a. Only collect and display essential personal data necessary for government services. 5. Secure Storage: a. Store personal data in encrypted databases with regular security updates and patches. 6. Legal Disclaimer: a. Clearly state the terms of use and privacy policies on the website.

questions.title: Responsive web design
questions.text: Responsive web design — A responsive web design (RWD) when the portal displays and works well (is navigable and usable) when accessed through a mobile device (e.g., smartphone, tablet). The portal could be provided through a regular web browser (responsive/adaptive website) or through a mobile application.
questions.what: A responsive web design (RWD) when the portal displays and works well (is navigable and usable) when accessed through a mobile device (e.g., smartphone, tablet). The portal could be provided through a regular web browser (responsive/adaptive website) or through a mobile application.
questions.why: RWD is an approach to web design aimed at crafting sites to provide an optimal viewing experience — easy reading and navigation with a minimum of resizing, panning, and scrolling — across a wide range of devices.

how.scoring_guidance: 1. Responsive Web Design: a. Implement a responsive web design adapting the layout and content based on the user's device 2. Mobile-Friendly Navigation: a. Simplify navigation for mobile users by using clear menus, intuitive icons, and a streamlined menu structure. 3. Readable Text and Images: a. Use legible font sizes and ensure images are appropriately sized for mobile screens. 4. Touch-Friendly Buttons: a. Design interactive elements, such as buttons and links, to be touch-friendly, ensuring they are large enough and well-spaced 5. Mobile Compatibility Testing: a. Regularly test the portal on different mobile devices and browsers to identify and address any issues related to display, functionality, or user experience.
